top.title: Light Switch: agent-designed micro-LED light patterns that stop spiral-wave arrhythmias in a heart-on-chip (merges seed B, 'Spiral-wave breaker' and 'Light Switch')
top.description: Thousands of 2D monodomain cardiac monolayers (Aliev-Panfilov plus a simplified channelrhodopsin light current, no-flux well boundary, optional fibrosis) step together in one JAX vmap on the GPU. The stimulus is a hard hardware constraint: a real addressable micro-LED matrix. Deng et al. 2026 (Advanced Science) built 48x32 (0.6 mm pitch) and 160x100 (0.9 mm pitch) matrices under human atrial CheRiff monolayers. An LLM agent writes light policies as short Python functions (input: voltage frame plus detected phase singularities; output: per-pixel irradiance and timing). CMA-ES (evosax) tunes their parameters, and each candidate is scored on about 1,000 reentry states per GPU call. Corrections to the ideators: (1) Deng et al. 2026 already closed an ML-plus-micro-LED loop in vitro. Their CNN finds the spiral core and a fixed rule fires one light line from the core to the nearest border; 73 events in 5 samples, over 80% terminated within 10 s. They also tested line pitches from 0.3 to 1.68 mm and found 0.8-0.9 mm optimal. This does not kill the idea. It gives a published baseline policy, real device geometry and a falsifiable validation target, which is whether simulation reproduces the 0.8-0.9 mm optimum. (2) DeTal 2022 reports single examples, not success rates, and no energy numbers. The contribution is therefore the first large-sample dose-vs-success statistics and a pitch co-design curve, plus agent-found policies that beat the line-to-border rule on dose or on multi-spiral states.

DeTal, Kaboudian, Fenton 2022 PNAS: FHN and Karma models, under 10% of the domain stimulated, a 9x9 electrode FHN case, no success rates over many states, no energy numbers: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9214532 . DeTal repo with FHN, BR, TP, OVVR and fhn-electrodes demos, no licence file: https://github.com/kaboudian/DefibrillationByTeleportation . Bingen et al. 2014 (Europe PMC abstract): 500 ms light pulses terminated reentry in 100% of CatCh neonatal rat atrial monolayers (n=31) vs 0% of controls (n=11): https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=EXT_ID:25082848%20AND%20SRC:MED&resultType=core&format=json . Majumder et al. 2018 eLife: Polygon400, CatCh, attract-anchor-drag; in-silico drag probability about 80% with continuous light: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6195347 . Junge et al. 2023: 16x16 micro-LEDs, 50x50 um, 140 um pitch, 450 nm, intensity droop with multiple pixels, no arrhythmia termination: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10636122/ . Babu and Pandit 2025: U-Net with a mesh electrode, Aliev-Panfilov and TP06, no numeric success rate in the abstract: https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.09806 . No paper combining GPU-batched tissues with policy search for spiral termination was found in one search.
top.main_risk: Model validity and spurious success. Aliev-Panfilov is phenomenological and not specific to hiPSC cells, and spirals can self-terminate on small domains (Deng saw about 10% self-terminate within 3 s). Mitigations: lock a sustained-reentry parameter regime first, always report results net of no-light controls, rerun winners at dx/2 and on held-out states and fibrosis maps, and claim only relative rankings and dose ratios. A secondary risk is that the novelty margin over Deng 2026 is the in-silico scale and dose minimisation, so the pitch must say that plainly.
top.headline_metric: Light dose (irradiance x lit area x time) needed for at least 90% termination on 1,000 held-out reentry states, best agent policy vs the Deng 2026 core-to-border line rule and vs a whole-field 500 ms pulse (Bingen 2014), on the 48x32, 0.6 mm-pitch grid. Reported as a ratio corrected for no-light self-termination. Validation figure: simulated success vs pitch (0.3-1.7 mm), checked against Deng's empirical 0.8-0.9 mm optimum. Throughput: simulated tissue-seconds per wall-clock second on GPU vs single-core CPU, measured on the day.

top.title: Sound-Sculpted Tissue: acoustic holograms optimised for where cells end up (merges 'SonoForm' and 'Sound-Sculpted Tissue')
top.description: A differentiable JAX chain runs angular-spectrum FFT propagation, then a Gor'kov radiation-force potential, then overdamped cell trajectories, then a soft Dice score against a tissue target such as a vessel-like branch or a ring. It is batched over targets x seeds x candidate phase plates. Plates are optimised end to end for the final simulated cell positions rather than for the pressure image. An LLM agent proposes objective and parameterisation hypotheses (penalising stray traps, quantised plate thickness levels, frequency), each run as a batched gradient experiment. The output is a printable plate thickness map. Correction: Melde et al. 2023 optimised the pressure field by projected gradient descent and used the Gor'kov potential only afterwards, to analyse traps. They did not simulate particle trajectories during optimisation, so the cell-level objective is a genuine gap. Start in 2D with a single plate; the 3D multi-hologram version is a stretch goal.

top.verified: Melde et al. 2023 Sci Adv: MSE to target pressure via projected gradient descent, Gor'kov potential used only to identify traps afterwards, no trajectory simulation in optimisation, 2.25 MHz, 2-3 holograms, C2C12 cells: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9908023/ . Shi, Fischer, Melde 2025 Biofabrication 17(3), C2C12 in GelMA at 40 million cells/ml average (viability figure not seen by me): https://heibib.ub.uni-heidelberg.de/search/Record/1939524172 . Diff-PAT, more than 8 dB over IASA: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8209099 . Physics-based acoustic holograms (holab): https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.03625 . One search for trajectory-aware hologram optimisation returned nothing matching. Not opened: the j-Wave repo and the Diff-PAT Zenodo licence (unverified by me).
top.main_risk: Acoustic streaming, which Ma et al. 2020 identify as what carries cells into the pattern, is not modelled, so a judge can question whether Gor'kov-only assembly predicts real outcomes. Gradients through long trajectories may explode; use short horizons or a potential-landscape proxy. The GPU workload is modest (batched FFTs), and the LLM loop is thinner than the gradient optimiser.
top.headline_metric: Mean Dice overlap between simulated cell density and target across a fixed suite of about 10 targets (including thin branches and loops): cell-aware plates vs IASA and pressure-matched plates at identical resolution. Plus plate evaluations per GPU-second vs CPU.

top.title: DLD chip designer: GPU lattice-Boltzmann search for pillar shapes that keep the cut-off with wider gaps (merges seed A, 'PillarForge' and 'Bump-array designer')
top.description: Thousands of periodic DLD unit cells are solved in a batched JAX D2Q9 lattice-Boltzmann or penalised-Stokes solver. Critical diameter comes from flux-lane estimates, spot-checked by finite-size particle tracing. An agent proposes shape families (triangles, I-shapes, asymmetric posts) and CMA-ES or MAP-Elites refines within each family. Validation: circular posts against the Davis fit Dc = 1.4 G eps^0.48. Output: a mask-ready array for circulating-tumour-cell or sepsis sorting. Correction: shape optimisation for DLD is crowded. Hyun et al. 2017 already did topology optimisation for wider gaps, Kabacaoglu and Biros used CMA-ES on B-spline posts, and DLDNN and Lee 2025 built surrogates. Novelty is limited to direct-simulation scale plus the hypothesis loop. XLB does not document vmap over geometries, so plan on a hand-written solver.
top.scores: hardware 5, AI-for-science loop 3, biotech 3, visual 4, parallelism 4, feasibility 4, honesty 4 (total 27/35)
top.verified: XLB: JAX, Warp and Neon backends, D2Q9, Apache-2.0; batching geometries via vmap not documented: https://github.com/Autodesk/XLB . Hyun et al. topology-optimised pillar, cited secondhand in DLDNN as widening the gap to reduce clogging (primary paper not opened, unverified): https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.14303 . Islam, Hasan, Liu 2025: ML surrogate for DLD design by cell mechanics: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.05649 . Kabacaoglu and Biros CMA-ES pillar optimisation: https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.08849 .
top.main_risk: Prior art is crowded, so judges may see it as a re-run of known DLD optimisation. Rigid 2D spheres ignore cell deformability and CTC-WBC size overlap. Lattice-Boltzmann accuracy in narrow gaps needs a grid-convergence check. It is less visually dramatic than the cardiac or acoustic demos.
top.headline_metric: Gap-widening factor at equal cut-off at eps = 0.1 (circle Dc/G divided by best shape Dc/G), with the circle validated against the Davis fit. Plus geometries fully characterised per GPU-hour vs single-core CPU.

top.title: OptoFit: AI co-design of optogenetic implants with GPU Monte Carlo light and heat in an atlas mouse brain
top.description: A per-emitter library of MCX (pmcx) GPU Monte Carlo fluence maps over position x angle x wavelength x optical-parameter set is built once. Light and Pennes heating are linear in power, so any multi-emitter design is a weighted sum of library maps, scored in batched JAX. An agent tests hypotheses such as whether 593 nm beats 473 nm per degree of heating, and MAP-Elites searches within each design family. The objective is coverage of the target nucleus above an opsin threshold with at most 1 °C heating. Correction: optode-layout optimisation by Monte Carlo already exists (a GATE study on fibre number, NA and arrangement in non-human-primate brain, plus a MATLAB 3D Monte Carlo platform with a mouse atlas). Novelty is narrower than claimed: the batched co-design under optical-property uncertainty plus the agent loop.
top.scores: hardware 5, AI-for-science loop 4, biotech 3, visual 4, parallelism 4, feasibility 3, honesty 4 (total 27/35)
top.verified: MCX: pip install pmcx, CUDA wheels for Linux and Windows only, NVIDIA GPU required, GPLv3: https://github.com/fangq/mcx . Stujenske et al. 2015: about 2.2 °C average and 4.1 °C peak for 10 mW at 532 nm through a 62 um fibre over 60 s; 532 nm heats nearly double 593 nm; 3 and 10 mW/mm2 contours in the EPD50 range; in vivo absorption about 5x in vitro, giving 300-500% more heating: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4512881/ . Prior-art search surfaced Monte Carlo optode-design and multiphysics probe models: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4679260 , https://doi.org/10.1088/1741-2552/aadf97 (abstracts seen via search snippets only).
top.main_risk: Optical properties are uncertain by a factor of several, which can change rankings; report worst case across both parameter sets. A threshold activation model ignores opsin kinetics and expression. Requires an NVIDIA GPU, and atlas plus MCX setup eats Saturday. The biotech teammate's input is lighter than in the cardiac or tissue ideas.
top.headline_metric: % of the target nucleus above the opsin threshold at peak temperature rise of 1 °C or less, AI design vs the best-placed single 200 um, NA 0.22 fibre, worst case over two optical-parameter sets. Plus designs scored per second on GPU vs CPU.

top.title: Wire the Dish: designing PDMS module-and-channel layouts that keep neuron-chip activity rich
top.description: Batched leaky integrate-and-fire networks, one per design x wiring seed x noise seed, with block connectivity derived from a manufacturable layout of modules and channels. Dynamical richness Θ is computed on the device. The gate is reproducing Yamamoto et al.'s qualitative ordering (no-bond, single-bond, triple-bond, merged). The agent then tests whether the 'verge of disconnection' optimum generalises to 2-16 modules, hierarchy and directional channels. Correction: axon growth is not simulated, so a layout maps to coupling only through assumed link probabilities. The output is a model-level test of a published principle plus candidate layouts to culture, not a validated chip.
top.scores: hardware 3, AI-for-science loop 4, biotech 4, visual 4, parallelism 4, feasibility 4, honesty 3 (total 26/35)
top.verified: Yamamoto et al. 2018 Sci Adv: four 200x200 um modules joined by 0, 1 or 3 lines; Θ is a product of two terms with 20 bins; richness peaks 'at the verge of physical disconnection'; the model is 4x25 LIF neurons: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6235526 . Not opened by me: Monma 2025, Forró 2018, the Cortical Labs CL1 report (unverified).
top.main_risk: Θ is noisy and sensitive to binning and burst thresholds, and the link from layout to connectivity is an assumption, so a sceptical judge can call the result a property of the model. The hardware angle (a PDMS layer) is weaker than an active device.
top.headline_metric: Θ of the best manufacturable agent layout vs Yamamoto's four-module single-bond layout re-simulated in the same engine, plus a yes/no with error bars on whether the Θ optimum sits at the weakest connecting coupling for 2-16 modules. Network-seconds per wall-clock second on GPU vs Brian2 on CPU.

verdict.recommended: Light Switch (rank 1): agent-designed micro-LED light patterns that stop spiral-wave arrhythmias in a simulated heart-on-chip. It covers all four of the team's constraints with the least strain. Hardware: a real addressable micro-LED matrix (Deng et al. 2026) as a hard constraint, plus a pitch co-design curve. AI for science: an LLM-written policy hypotheses loop with a CMA-ES inner loop and held-out validation. Biotech: optogenetic cardiomyocytes, opsin, arrhythmia induction. Visual: a wall of spirals going dark. The GPU story is honest (thousands of independent tissues per call), it builds without wet-lab data, and Deng 2026 hands the team a published baseline rule (core-to-border line) and an empirical pitch optimum (0.8-0.9 mm) that the simulation can be checked against. The parallelism has a clear measured metric. The main honesty caveat is that claims stay at relative dose and policy rankings within a 2D phenomenological model.
verdict.plan_30h:
Roles: CS = solver, agent and renderer; Bio = parameters, baselines, validation targets and the pitch narrative.

Sat 11:00-14:00
- CS: batched JAX Aliev-Panfilov on a circular no-flux well mask (about 256^2 grid, jit plus vmap over a batch dimension). Add S1-S2 spiral induction, a random multi-spiral generator, and a phase-singularity detector (phase angle from (V, v), winding number).
- Bio: from Deng 2026, Bingen 2014 and Majumder 2018, fix target spiral period, APD and conduction velocity. Fix the light-current form: a simplified ChR2/CheRiff depolarising current with an irradiance-to-conductance curve, capped at Deng's maximum of 116 mW/cm2. Define the dose metric and the 'terminated' criterion: no phase singularity and no activity for X ms.
- Gate at 14:00: no-light controls keep reentry going for at least 10 s simulated in at least 90% of states.

Sat 14:00-18:00
- Encode the mLED grid as the only actuator: 48x32 at 0.6 mm pitch with a configurable pitch, and optional intensity droop as more pixels light.
- Baselines, batched over about 1,000 states:
  - a whole-field pulse duration sweep (expect long pulses to work and short ones to fail, qualitatively matching Bingen);
  - Deng's core-to-nearest-border line rule;
  - a DeTal-style refractory-tail rule.
- First GPU vs single-core NumPy throughput number (tissue-seconds per second).
- Freeze the train and held-out state splits.

Sat 18:00-23:00
- Agent harness: the LLM writes policy(frame, singularities, t) -> pixel irradiance in a sandboxed API, with an evosax CMA-ES inner loop over its numeric parameters.
- The harness returns success rate, dose, time to termination and failure thumbnails, and logs a hypothesis tree.
- Seed hypotheses: core spot vs line-to-border, timed refractory-tail hits, sweeping bars for multi-spiral states, minimal pixel subsets.
- Launch overnight in the background with logging, and launch the pitch sweep (0.3-1.7 mm) for the baselines in parallel.

Sun 08:00-12:00
- Score finalists on held-out states, fibrosis maps (5-20% inexcitable cells) and a dx/2 grid.
- Compute dose ratios net of self-termination.
- Pitch co-design curve: does the simulated optimum land near Deng's 0.8-0.9 mm? Report it either way.
- Final throughput benchmark, with batch-size scaling up to the maximum the GPU holds.

Sun 12:00-16:00
- Live demo: an 8x8 tile wall streamed from the GPU, with phase singularities as dots and the LED grid overlay flashing.
- A 'defibrillate' button runs the agent policy vs Deng's rule side by side with a dose counter.
- Side panels: the agent notebook, the dose-vs-success Pareto front and the pitch curve.
- Record a fallback video by 15:00.

Sun 16:00-18:00
- Slides around one headline ratio, plus a 'can claim / cannot claim' slide (2D monodomain, phenomenological, relative rankings only, wet-lab test plan from Bio). Rehearse twice.

Headline metric: light dose for at least 90% termination on held-out states, agent policy vs Deng 2026's core-to-border rule and vs a whole-field 500 ms pulse, as a ratio. Secondary: the success-vs-pitch curve against Deng's empirical 0.8-0.9 mm optimum, and GPU vs CPU tissue-seconds per second.
killed: Seed C, drug cardiotoxicity screen on the same tissue model: two-variable excitable models have no ion channels, so drug block cannot be represented honestly, and CiPA population-of-models work (e.g. 1,213 O'Hara-Rudy models x 62 compounds) already owns this space; see https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5563361 (search snippet).

Seed D, programmable living display: no real hardware device, and differentiable inverse design of gene networks for cell-cluster morphogenesis already exists (Deshpande, Mottes et al., arXiv 2407.06295, seen in search results).
Seed E, self-driving lab on a digital microfluidic chip: droplet routing and scheduling is a long-established biochip-CAD problem with weak GPU parallelism and a weak visual.

Seed B, low-energy defibrillation with electrodes: merged into Light Switch, where the optogenetic micro-LED version has a real device (Deng 2026) and in-vitro baselines, while bidomain virtual-electrode effects make electrode claims less defensible.
Seed A, AI-designed microfluidic sorter: merged into the DLD chip designer (rank 3).
PillarForge and Bump-array designer: merged into the DLD chip designer.
Spiral-wave breaker: merged into Light Switch (rank 1).

Through-skull focus designer: the hardest build (25.3 GB data, 3D runs that j-Wave could not complete for benchmarks 8-9 in 2022, vmap unverified), and with a linear model phase conjugation already maximises single-point focus, so gains are thin in 30 h.
Bionic-eye layout lab: very close Beyeler-lab prior art (encoders, human-in-the-loop, electrode arrangement) and a GPU workload so light that compute-minded judges see the GPU as optional.

SpikeSteer: Jaxley has no built-in extracellular stimulation, so the core physics must be written from scratch, and per the ideator, Ronchi et al. 2019 found simultaneous multi-electrode stimulation gave no efficiency gain (not re-opened by me); it also needs neuroscience depth the team may lack.

Sperm Slalom: its validation baseline fails as specified. Ahmadkhani et al. 2023's sinusoidal-channel gain (92.4% vs 80.8% progressive motility) depends on upstream flow of about 50 um/s, which the ideator made optional, and the curvature-detachment wall rules are unestablished (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10590352).
